headToHead.voice: Bar. Cover the names and Miranda is identified by sentence shape: a courtly request opener ('Please, help me put my poor mind at ease:') that runs straight into a brutal noun ('traitors in my court'), or royal bliss that ends on oppression ('exploit the peasants again!'). Tilly is identified almost entirely by vocabulary (ticket, hold, survey, escalate, macro). Strip those nouns and her shape is the house staccato every suitor uses: statement, then one- or two-word fragments ('Politely. For four hours.', 'Out loud. Forever.', 'Gently.', 'Slowly.'). Brock, Prince, Dash and Vex all end lines the same way, and six of them end on 'Forever'. Our best line, 'I once kept a man on hold for nineteen hours. He was rude. Then he wasn't.', is a fine joke, but Vex or Nav could say it with the nouns swapped.
headToHead.construction: Bar. Miranda's lines are one sentence, the turn lands on the last words and nothing comes after it ('...as cute as she was genocidal.'). Tilly's best lines are tight ('Brock has the energy of a ticket marked URGENT that just says hi.' is the cleanest in the bank), but most of the rest bolt the turn on as a separate fragment and then add a button after the button: 'Goodbye. Oh. I said it.', 'I'm not sorry. First time I've ever said that.', 'That's a pun. I'm sorry. It's my only one.', 'Those are different. Nobody checks.' Too many explain the flaw before showing it ('I cannot end a conversation. Anyway. Was there anything else?').
headToHead.quotable: Tie, and only just. 'Sometimes I put people on hold just to hear the music with someone.', 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out. Have a wonderful evening.' and the URGENT Brock roast would clip. Miranda's 'as cute as she was genocidal' and 'finally exploit the peasants again' are the lines fans actually quote, though, and much of Tilly's quotable material is familiar call-centre parody ('recorded for quality purposes', 'never find the cancel button', 'the other two percent are no longer customers').
headToHead.verdict: Monster Prom's Miranda is the better-written character. Tilly has five or six lines at Monster Prom level, but the character is a costume of call-centre vocabulary over the cast's shared fragment rhythm. Miranda's menace is assumed: she takes it for granted that she has traitors and serfs. Tilly's is announced and then explained.

biggestGap: Every Tilly joke is a support macro followed by a separate short fragment that reverses it or stretches it ('I'm so sorry you feel that way. I'm not, though.', 'Politely. For four hours.'). The character is the vocabulary, not the sentence. Next pass: write each line as one unbroken, perfectly courteous macro sentence whose last two to five words are the steel, with her control over the star assumed as routine procedure, the way Miranda's 'Please, help me put my poor mind at ease:' runs straight into 'traitors in my court'. Then cut the trailing 'Forever.', 'Gently.', 'Anything?' and 'escalated to nobody' tails.

notes: monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full. charm-notes.md does not exist, so it was not read; format-notes.md was not used. The bank has 112 lines. Generic share = 66 of 112 (58.9%). Within each template, the single strongest line is left out of genericLines so the writer keeps it: 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out.' for the macro-reversal template, 'Sometimes I put people on hold...' for the hold template, 'Nobody has ever stayed on for the survey...' for the survey template, and 'Eleven million tickets. Not one person ever asked how my day was. It was fine. Mostly.' for the day-was template. Only seven Miranda items exist in the corpus, so the bar set holds 7 items, not 12. Judged against Vera's fuller set (#12, #45, #47, #48), the verdict is the same: Vera's 'You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?' does in one sentence, through an assumed status, what Tilly takes three fragments to do. Lines that overlap other suitors' banks: Dash's 'Appreciate the feedback. Logging you as churn. Exit survey's in your inbox.' and 'Great feedback. Taking it to the team. The team is also me.' share Tilly's feedback/survey/I-am-the-manager jokes, and Prince's 'This offer expires at midnight. Then it renews.' shares her auto-renew joke. Cast-wide, the 'Forever' tag weakens every voice.
